entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Rupa Bai Furdoonji was an Indian Parsi doctor who revolutionized the field of anesthesiology in the early 20th century. Born in the 1880s in Bombay (now Mumbai), India, she studied medicine at the prestigious Grant Medical College and became one of the first female anesthetists in India. Rupa Bai Furdoonji's pioneering work in using chloroform as an anesthetic in India had a lasting impact on the field of medicine, paving the way for future generations of female anesthesiologists.


Rupa Bai Furdoonji's achievements extend beyond her professional contributions, as she also played a significant role in promoting women's rights and education in India. Her legacy continues to inspire healthcare professionals and feminist scholars alike.


As a trailblazer for women in medicine, Rupa Bai Furdoonji's story serves as a testament to the power of perseverance and determination in the face of societal obstacles.
